laki_eruption.name: Laki fissure eruption and the Mist Hardships

history.disputes: England's excess deaths (estimated around 20,000 in 1783-84) and the link to the Egyptian famine (Volney's contemporary claim that a sixth of Egypt died) are model- or source-dependent. Claims that Laki caused the French Revolution are not supported; the 1788 French harvest failure had other causes (notably a July 1788 hailstorm).
Estimates of enslaved people who escaped range from about 20,000 to far higher; the weight of ideology, taxation and land hunger among Patriot motives remains debated.
The death toll (1-10 million) and the proportion attributable to Company policy are debated.

indian_removal_act.name: Indian Removal and the Trail of Tears

history.disputes: Death tolls are uncertain; about 4,000 of roughly 16,000 Cherokee removed is the usual estimate; overall about 60,000 to 80,000 people were removed. Recent historians (Saunt, Ostler) describe removal as ethnic cleansing.
Treating 1566 as a turning point is a historiographical convention.
Monetarist (Friedman and Schwartz), gold-standard (Eichengreen) and hegemonic-stability (Kindleberger) explanations weigh the causes differently.
Keynes's view that reparations were ruinous is challenged by historians who argue they were payable and that the treaty's failure was political.
Ethiopian casualty totals for 1935-41 are uncertain; the Ethiopian government's postwar claim of about 760,000 dead is not verified. Yekatit 12 estimates range from a few thousand to around 19,000.

Nanjing death tolls range from tens of thousands to over 300,000 depending on area, period and categories counted; the subject remains politically contested in Japan and China. Chinese wartime deaths are estimated at about 14-20 million.
Start dates differ by region (1931 Manchuria, 1937 China, 1939 Europe, 1941 Pacific); casualty totals are estimates.

Historians debate the timing of the decision for total extermination (summer-autumn 1941 to early 1942) and the balance between central orders and local initiative. Estimates for murdered Roma and Sinti range from about 200,000 to 500,000.

Historians differ on the weight of crop failure (Tauger) versus market and policy failure (Sen) and on the personal role of Churchill's War Cabinet in refusing imports; death toll estimates range from about 1.5 to 3 million.

atomic_bombings.name: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

history.disputes: Whether the bombs, the Soviet declaration of war or both caused Japan's surrender, whether an invasion would otherwise have been necessary, and whether alternatives (demonstration, modified surrender terms) existed are long-running debates. Korean death estimates are uncertain, commonly in the tens of thousands across both cities.
The date and form of the Bois Caïman ceremony are debated; the 1804 killings are interpreted variously as retaliation, security policy or massacre (Dubois 2004, Geggus 2002).
